mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in retail sales (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals a weakening consumer demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are negatively impacted.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the correlation between RSAFS declines and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in a month signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market sentiment improves.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained low inflation environment (CPIAUCSL below 2% for 3 consecutive months) signals a potential for monetary easing, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real interest rates decline.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the correlation between low CPIAUCSL and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% in a month signals a strengthening demand in the housing sector, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic activity and related sectors benefit.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the correlation between HOUST increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2% in the same month, it signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the joint effect of PAYEMS and UNRATE changes on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a strengthening economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings and economic outlook improve.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of instances despite the signal, or the correlation between GDPC1 increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
